body.x: At the world’s largest IT and electronics exhibition, CES 2026, global AR communication technology company LEION (developed by LLVision) captured widespread attention with the unveiling of its next-generation AR smart glasses, ‘LEION HEY2.’ Long lines formed in front of the booth as visitors waited to try the device, while scenes of people speaking different languages and communicating smoothly were repeatedly witnessed across the exhibition floor. As translated subtitles appeared in real time before users’ eyes, many remarked that “AI has truly become part of human perception.”

LEION HEY2 positions itself as the world’s first “professional AR translation glasses.” While smartphone apps and conventional AR glasses have treated translation as an auxiliary feature, HEY2 was designed from the outset specifically for face-to-face multilingual communication. When a conversation partner speaks in a foreign language, the audio is converted into subtitles within an average of 0.5 seconds and displayed directly in the wearer’s field of view. Notably, the other party does not need to wear the glasses; they can follow the translated conversation in real time via a smartphone screen. This enables both sides to maintain eye contact and converse naturally without looking down at a phone or wearing earphones. At CES 2026, the device was widely described as “a product that redefines the direction of translation devices.”

body.x: “Conversations Don’t Break” — The Advantage of Subtitle-Based Real-Time Translation

The most enthusiastically received feature at the show was the continuity of conversation. Unlike conventional translation devices that deliver translated content only after a speaker finishes talking, HEY2 continuously assembles and displays text in real time as speech progresses. Even before a sentence is completed, users can grasp the context, preventing interruptions in conversation. Many hands-on users commented that “being able to see the translation as it forms makes responses much faster.”

This capability is enabled by HEY2’s dual-eye optical display and head-up interaction structure. Subtitle size and position can be adjusted and remain consistently within the user’s field of view. Beyond general users, these characteristics also make the device valuable as a real-time captioning aid for people with hearing impairments or partial hearing loss.

body.x: "Over 100 Languages and Three-Way Translation — AI Proven in the Real World"

In terms of functionality, HEY2 ranks among the most advanced wearable translation devices currently available. It supports two-way translation across more than 100 languages and dialects, can recognize up to five languages simultaneously, and enables three-way multilingual conversations. Its ability to perform reliably even in noisy environments such as CES is attributed to four built-in microphones, 360-degree spatial audio recognition, and a forward-facing speaker focus algorithm covering approximately 60 degrees. These features suppress ambient noise and isolate the voice of the conversation partner, enhancing translation accuracy. Neural network-based noise reduction further ensures stable performance in exhibition halls, streets, and meeting rooms.

HEY2 goes beyond translation alone. With Free Talk mode, two-way communication is possible even when the conversation partner is not wearing the glasses. The user reads translated subtitles, while their own speech is output as translated audio through the smartphone app. In presentation or lecture settings, the teleprompter function displays scripts as subtitles, enabling smoother and more natural delivery.

The AI Q&A assistant, activated by touching the glasses’ temple, also attracted attention. It provides instant responses to simple questions, explanations of terms, and multilingual meeting summaries, complementing the translation experience. The company stated that while the initial model prioritizes stability, more advanced AI engines will be introduced gradually after CES.

body.x: "Camera-Free AR Glasses — Trust Built Through Privacy-Centric Design"

Another defining feature of HEY2 is the absence of a camera. By deliberately excluding video capture and external speakers and focusing solely on voice-based translation, the device minimizes privacy concerns in business meetings, exhibitions, and public spaces. All data processing is conducted via Microsoft Azure-based cloud infrastructure in compliance with GDPR standards, and users retain control over managing and deleting translation records.

LEION previously launched HEY2 in South Korea as its first global market. As access to the U.S. market has become more challenging for Chinese technology companies, South Korea has emerged as a strategic testbed for global expansion. With high technology adoption rates and a strong base of early adopters, Korea was selected as the initial launch market. LEION currently operates a local office in Korea and has reportedly received over 200 units in pre-orders through partnerships with local distributors. Building on this track record, the company plans to accelerate expansion into North America, Europe, and the Middle East.

The impression left by LEION HEY2 at CES 2026 was unmistakable. AI is no longer confined to screens; it is evolving into physical intelligence that extends human perception. Scenes of people wearing smart glasses with real-time subtitles while conversing effortlessly across language barriers became one of the exhibition’s most symbolic moments. By demonstrating AI that truly works in real-world settings, LEION’s CES 2026 debut signaled the next stage of global communication.
